rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught Adam the names of every terrestrial animal and bird, naming creatures such as horses, mules, and donkeys individually.
rows.anchor: فعلم آدم، عليه السلام، أسماءها، فقال: يا آدم، هذا فرس، وهذا بغل، وهذا حمار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God displayed the named creatures to the angels on earth and challenged them to identify them if truthful about the coming corruption and bloodshed.
rows.anchor: ثم عرض أهل تلك الأسماء على الملائكة الذين هم فى الأرض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor recalled to Israel's ancestors includes rescue from Pharaoh, destruction of their enemy, the parted sea, manna and quails, shade, a night light, twelve springs, and the Torah's guidance to worship God alone.
rows.anchor: فكانت النعمة حين أنجاهم من آل فرعون، وأهلك عدوهم، وحين فرق البحر لهم، وحين أنزل عليهم المن والسلوى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel's covenant in the Torah required worshipping God without partners and believing in Muhammad, the prophets, and the Scripture; the cited covenant also enjoins prayer, almsgiving, supporting messengers, and a good loan.
rows.anchor: عهد إليهم فى التوراة أن يعبدوه ولا يشركوا به شيئا، وأن يؤمنوا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Israel fulfilled the covenant, God promised forgiveness and Paradise; the passage in 5:12 is cited as God's fulfillment of that promise.
rows.anchor: يعنى المغفرة والجنة، فعاهدهم إن أوفوا له بما قال المغفرة والجنة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel instead disbelieved in Muhammad and Jesus, and fearing God means fearing Him concerning Muhammad, since whoever denies Muhammad faces Hell.
rows.anchor: فكفروا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وبعيسى، عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God is specifically about Muhammad: whoever denies him will be in Hell.
rows.anchor: وإياى فخافون فى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، فمن كذب به فله النار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews told some of Muhammad's companions that Muhammad was true and urged them to follow him, yet the Jews themselves left their own selves by not following him.
rows.anchor: إن محمدا حق فاتبعوه ترشدوا، فقال الله عز وجل لليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah contains a clear account and description of Muhammad, so the Jews should understand and follow him.
rows.anchor: يعنى التوراة فيها بيان أمر محمد ونعته،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking help for the Hereafter means patiently observing the obligations and guarding the five prayers at their appointed times.
rows.anchor: الخمس حافظوا عليها فى مواقيتها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qibla change from Jerusalem to the Kaaba was burdensome for Jews including Jaddi ibn Akhtab and Saʿid ibn ʿAmr the poet, but not for humble believers.
rows.anchor: فكبر ذلك على اليهود منهم: جدى بن أخطب، وسعيد بن عمرو الشاعر وغيرهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humble are believing people for whom the qibla change was not difficult; they know with certainty that they will meet their Lord in the Hereafter and return to Him for recompense.
rows.anchor: يعنى إلا على المتواضعين من المؤمنين، لم يكبر عليهم تحويل القبلة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “think” here means knowing with certainty that they will meet their Lord in the Hereafter and return to Him for recompense.
rows.anchor: يعنى يعلمون يقينا { أنهم ملاقو ربهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the wilderness, the Israelites asked Moses for water; God told him to strike a light, square stone, from which twelve springs flowed, one for each tribe, without their drinking places mixing.
rows.anchor: وكان الحجر خفيفا مربعا، فضربه، { فانفجرت منه } من الحجر { اثنتا عشرة عينا } ، فرووا بإذن الله عز وجل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each tribe knew its own drinking place; the people were to eat manna and quails and drink the springs as lawful, wholesome provision from God.
rows.anchor: وكانوا اثنى عشر سبطا، لكل سبط من بنى إسرائيل عين تجرى على حدة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on corruption means not acting sinfully on earth; they saved manna and quails for the next day, violating the command not to hoard it.
rows.anchor: فرفعوا من المن والسلوى لغد، فذلك قوله سبحانه: ولا تطغوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The linked command in 20:81 means they must not save any manna for the next day; Moses carried the stone when traveling, and springs would be set flowing from it.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا ترفعوا منه لغد، وكان موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا ظعن حمل الحجر معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asked about clothing, God made the Israelites' garments grow with their children, remain on adults, and neither tear, wear out, nor become dirty; a pillar of light illuminated their journeys at night without moonlight.
rows.anchor: فجعلت الثياب تطول مع أولادهم، وتبقى على كبارهم، ولا تمزق ولا تبلى ولا تدنس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After tiring of manna and quails, the Israelites asked Moses for earth's produce; “fūm” means garlic.
rows.anchor: فومها } ، يعنى الثوم، { وعدسها وبصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses rebuked them for exchanging the inferior produce of the earth for the better manna and quails, and told them to go down to a city where they could obtain what they requested.
rows.anchor: يقول: الذى هو دون المن والسلوى من نبات الأرض { بالذي هو خير } ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humiliation imposed on the Jews means the jizya, and neediness means poverty; they incurred God's anger.
rows.anchor: يعنى على اليهود الذلة، وهى الجزية، { والمسكنة } ، يعنى الفقر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs of God they disbelieved in mean the Qur'an; they killed prophets unjustly because they disobeyed and transgressed in their religion.
rows.anchor: بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله } ، يعنى القرآن، { ويقتلون النبيين بغير الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the five prayers, Muhammad and his companions prayed two units at dawn and dusk in Mecca; after the Night Ascent five prayers were prescribed, with two units for travelers and four for residents.
rows.anchor: كانوا بمكة يصلون ركعتين بالغداة وركعتين بالعشى، فلما عرج بالنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى السماء ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After migrating to Medina, the Prophet was ordered to pray toward Jerusalem so the People of the Book would not deny him, since they found his description in the Torah; Muslims prayed that way for seventeen months, while the Ansar had done so for two years before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: فصلى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه قبل بيت المقدس من أول مقدمه المدينة سبعة عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kaaba was the Prophet's preferred qibla; he told Gabriel he wished God would turn him away from the Jews' qibla, and Gabriel said he was only a servant and advised him to ask God.
rows.anchor: وددت أن ربى صرفنى عن قبلة اليهود إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel ascended while the Prophet kept looking toward heaven in hope of an answer; in Rajab, during the first prayer and two months before Badr, God ordered him to face the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله عز وجل فى رجب عند صلاة الأولى قبل قتال بدر بشهرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan polytheists claimed the Prophet had changed direction from longing for his ancestral birthplace and would return to their religion; Muqatil calls this foolishness.
rows.anchor: قال مشركو مكة: قد تردد على أمره واشتاق إلى مولد آبائه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fools are Meccan polytheists who asked what turned the Muslims from their former qibla; east and west belong to God, who guides whom He wills to Islam.
rows.anchor: يعنى مشركي مكة، { ما ولاهم } ، يقول: ما صرفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews Marhab, Rafiʿ, and Rabiʿa told Muʿadh that Muhammad left their qibla out of envy and that it was the prophets' qibla; Muʿadh answered that his community was right and just, prompting this revelation.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن اليهود منهم مرحب، ورافع، وربيعة، قالوا لمعاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Middle” means just, as in 68:28, where the middlemost brother means the most just, and 5:89, where the middle food means the most just portion.
rows.anchor: يعنى عدلا، نظيرها فى ن والقلم، قوله سبحانه: قال أوسطهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community of Muhammad will testify justly in the Hereafter between the prophets and their peoples.
rows.anchor: يعنى أمة محمد تشهد بالعدل فى الآخرة بين الأنبياء وبين أممهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community's testimony concerning people means testifying whether the messengers delivered God's message to their peoples.
rows.anchor: يعني على الرسل هل بلغت الرسالة عن ربها إلى أممهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger who will testify concerning the community is Muhammad, who will testify that he delivered the message to them.
rows.anchor: يعني على أمته أنه بلغهم الرسالة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The former qibla was Jerusalem; “that We may know” means that God may see who follows Muhammad in the qibla and who among the Jews turns back to the former religion.
rows.anchor: يعني بيت المقدس، { إلا لنعلم } ، إلا لنرى { من يتبع الرسول } ، يعني محمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qibla change was difficult for Jews but not for those God guided.
rows.anchor: يعني القبلة حين صرفها عن بيت المقدس إلى الكعبة، فعظمت على اليهود،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huyayy ibn Akhtab and his companions challenged Muslims over whether their former prayers toward Jerusalem were guidance or error; Muslims answered that guidance is what God commanded and error what He prohibited.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن حيى بن أخطب اليهودى وأصحابه قالوا للمسلمين: أخبرونا عن صلاتكم نحو بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Saʿd ibn Zurarah, al-Baraʾ ibn Maʿrur, and other Muslims died before the qibla change, their relatives asked the Prophet how their former prayers should be regarded.
rows.anchor: وكان قد مات قبل أن تحول القبلة إلى الكعبة: أسعد بن زرارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God would not let your faith be lost” means that He accepted the prayers of those who died facing Jerusalem before the qibla changed.
rows.anchor: يعني إيمان صلاتكم نحو بيت المقدس، يقول: لقد تقبلت منهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is compassionate and merciful to people because He accepted those prayers before the qibla change.
rows.anchor: يعنى يرق لهم، { رحيم } [آية: 143] حين قبلها منهم قبل تحويل القبلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should seek the Hereafter by patiently observing obligations and the five prayers toward the Kaaba at their appointed times, after Jews taunted them for abandoning the former qibla; God is with those patient in duty and prayer.
rows.anchor: استعينوا على طلب الآخرة بالصبر على الفرائض والصلوات الخمس فى مواقيتها نحو الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on calling those slain in God's path dead was revealed about fourteen Muslims killed at Badr: eight Ansar and six emigrants, whom people had called dead.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى قتلى بدر من المسلمين، وهم أربعة عشر رجلا من المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Badr martyrs are alive and provided for in Paradise with God, though people cannot perceive this; the dwelling place of martyrs' souls is Sidrat al-Muntaha in the Garden of Refuge.
rows.anchor: { بل أحياء } مرزوقون فى الجنة عند الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trial of fear and hunger means drought, and the loss of wealth, lives, and fruits means lack of rain; the patient are promised Paradise for enduring this affliction.
rows.anchor: يعنى القحط، { ونقص من الأموال والأنفس والثمرات } ، يعنى قحط المطر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those afflicted respond that they belong to God and return to Him; the Lord's prayers mean forgiveness, as in 9:103, where praying upon people means seeking forgiveness and the prayer is a supplication that comforts them.
rows.anchor: يعنى مغفرة، كقوله سبحانه: وصل عليهم يعنى استغفر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy and guidance here describe those who say the return formula when afflicted.
rows.anchor: { ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون } [آية: 157] للاسترجاع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concealment was prompted when Muʿadh ibn Jabal, Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, and Haritha ibn Zayd asked Jews about Muhammad and stoning; Jews including Kaʿb al-Ashraf and Ibn Suriyya concealed the answers.
rows.anchor: سألوا اليهود عن أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن الرجم وغيره فكتموهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proofs concealed were what God explained in the Torah, including stoning and lawful and unlawful matters; the guidance was the Torah's information about Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يعنى ما بين الله عز وجل فى التوراة، يعنى الرجم والحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The linked statement in 29:49 calls those who deny God's signs wrongdoers, meaning people who reject the Torah.
rows.anchor: وما يجحد بآياتنآ أى بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا الظالمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “cursers” are all creatures except jinn and humans: they hear a disbeliever cry after being struck in the grave and curse him for withholding their sustenance by his sin.
rows.anchor: فيصيح ويسمع صوته الخليقة كلهم، غير الجن والإنس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers among the People of the Torah are excepted if they repent of unbelief, do righteous deeds, and disclose Muhammad's status to people; God then pardons them.
rows.anchor: أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم للناس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who die as unbelievers are cursed by God, angels, and all people, meaning all believers; abiding therein means abiding in the curse and in Hell, with no easing or delay of punishment.
rows.anchor: يعنى المؤمنين جميعا، { خالدين فيها } ، يعنى فى اللعنة واللعنة النار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to the People of the Book declares that their Lord is one and God unifies Himself as the sole deity, the Merciful and Compassionate.
rows.anchor: يقول: ربكم رب واحد، فوحد نفسه تبارك اسمه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hajj and umrah are obligatory; complete them from their appointed stations without making lawful what is forbidden. Umrah is also said to be the lesser pilgrimage, and completion requires sincere ihram without worldly admixture.
rows.anchor: فريضتان واجبتان، ويقال: العمرة هى الحج الأصغر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People in pre-Islamic times associated partners when entering ihram, so God commanded the Prophet and Muslims to perform both rites solely for Him and warned against permitting forbidden acts.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أهل الجاهلية كانوا يشركون فى إحرامهم، فأمر الله عز وجل النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ihsar” means being detained, as in 2:273 and 17:8, where the same root describes people detained in God's path and Hell as a prison.
rows.anchor: إن حبسكم فى إحرامكم بحج أو بعمرة كسر أو مرض أو عدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If illness, injury, or an enemy blocks a pilgrim in ihram, the pilgrim remains there and sends whatever hady is available or its price to buy a sacrifice; after it is slaughtered, the pilgrim exits ihram there.
rows.anchor: فليقم محرما مكانه ويبعث ما استيسر من الهدي أو بثمن الهدي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pilgrim must not shave until the sacrifice reaches its place, which means it enters Mecca; after it is slaughtered, the pilgrim exits ihram.
rows.anchor: يعنى حتى يدخل الهدي مكة، فإذا نحر الهدي حل من إحرامه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Hudaybiyya, Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra was in umrah and had many lice at the front of his head; the Prophet asked whether they troubled him, and when Kaʿb said yes, ordered him to shave, occasioning the verse about illness or head injury.
rows.anchor: أن كعب بن عجرة الأنصارى كان محرما بعمرة عام الحديبية، فرأى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The head-injury expiation can be three fasting days, consecutive or separated, or charity of half a measure of wheat for each of six poor people.
rows.anchor: فعليه فدية صيام ثلاثة أيام إن شاء متتابعا، وإن شاء متقطعا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacrificial expiation means a sheep, cow, or camel slaughtered and given to Meccan poor, with none eaten by the pilgrim; Kaʿb chose a cow.
rows.anchor: يعنى شاة أو بقرة أو بعيرا ينحره، ثم يطعمه المساكين بمكة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When safe from an enemy's blockade, a person enjoying umrah before Hajj intends Hajj and enters Mecca in umrah during Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, or the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijja; the minimum hady is a sheep, which the pilgrim may eat from and share.
rows.anchor: يقول: وهو يريد الحج، فإن دخل مكة وهو محرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra, Salman, and Abu al-Arbad told the Prophet they could not find a sacrifice and would fast three days; the command to fast was revealed concerning them.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو هريرة، وسلمان، وأبو العرباض للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنا لا نجد الهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three Hajj fasts are during the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijja through the Day of Arafah; if Arafah is the third day, the fast is complete. The seven days may be fasted en route or at home, continuously or separately.
rows.anchor: فى عشر الأضحى فى أول يوم من العشر إلى يوم عرفة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamattuʿ and its substitute fasts apply only to those whose homes are outside all of the Sacred Precinct; its residents have neither tamattuʿ nor the fast.
rows.anchor: يعنى من لم يكن منزله فى أرض الحرم كله، فمن كان أهله فى أرض الحرم، فلا متعة عليه ولا صوم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known Hajj months are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijja; someone entering ihram outside them has missed the Sunnah and should make it umrah.
rows.anchor: فليحرم فى شوال، أو فى ذى القعدة، أو فى عشر ذى الحجة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To make Hajj binding means to enter ihram for Hajj; “rafath” means intercourse, as in 2:187, “fusuq” means abusive speech, and “jidal” means disputation, as in 40:4.
rows.anchor: يقول: فمن أحرم { فيهن الحج } أى الحج، { فلا رفث } ، يعنى فلا جماع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disputation means arguing in anger while in ihram or angering one's companion; whoever does this must feed a poor person.
rows.anchor: يعنى ولا مراء، كقوله سبحانه: ما يجادل في آيات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet ordered those without a sacrificial animal to leave ihram and make their rite umrah; people who had declared Hajj objected, and this was their disputation with him.
rows.anchor: من لم يكن معه هدي فليحل من إحرامه، وليجعلها عمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows and rewards every good act, including refraining from intercourse, sinful speech, and disputation during Hajj.
rows.anchor: { وما تفعلوا من خير } ، يعنى مما نهى من ترك الرفث والفسوق والجدال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pilgrims from Yemen and elsewhere used to travel without provisions and wrong people along the road, so they were told to carry enough food to avoid asking others and not oppress those they pass.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن ناسا من أهل اليمن وغيرهم كانوا يحجون بغير زاد، وكانوا يصيبون من أهل الطريق ظلما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa is the best provision, and “people of understanding” means people possessing intellect.
rows.anchor: وخير الزاد التقوى، يقول الله تبارك اسمه: التقوى خير زاد من غيره،

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When the verse was revealed, the Prophet said to carry enough provision to preserve one's dignity among people and that the best provision is taqwa.
rows.anchor: تزودوا ما تكفون به وجوهكم عن الناس، وخير ما تزودتم التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Abu Bakr and his son Abd al-Rahman: Abu Bakr swore not to maintain ties with him until he became Muslim, while people held that an oath must be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى أبى بكر الصديق، رضى الله عنه، وفى ابنه عبد الرحمن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not swear to abandon obedience, kinship, visiting or speaking to a neighbor, or reconciling people; reconciliation, piety, and maintaining ties are better than fulfilling an oath to sin.
rows.anchor: لا تحلفوا ألا تصلوا القرابة: { أن تبروا وتتقوا } الله { وتصلحوا بين الناس } ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the oath and knows it; this prohibition preceded the revelation of expiation in 5:89.
rows.anchor: { والله سميع } لليمين؛ لقولهم: حلفنا عليها، { عليم } [آية: 224]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A careless oath is one a person swears believing it true but being mistaken; God does not hold the person to it, and no expiation is due.
rows.anchor: وهو الرجل يحلف على أمر يرى أنه فيه صادق وهو مخطئ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the heart earns means an intentionally false oath, sworn while knowing it is a lie; that oath requires expiation.
rows.anchor: يعنى بما عقدت قلوبكم من المأثم، يعنى اليمين الكاذبة التى حلف عليها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forgiving by pardoning the mistaken oath and forbearing by not imposing expiation for it.
rows.anchor: { والله غفور } ، يعنى ذا تجاوز عن اليمين التى حلف عليها، { حليم } [آية: 225]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to leave outstanding usury concerned four Thaqif brothers—Masʿud, Habib, Rabiʿa, and Abd Yalil—who lent at interest to Banu al-Mughira; after the conquest of Taif, Thaqif claimed its interest while waiving debts owed by them, and the dispute reached the Meccan governor Attab ibn Asid, who wrote the Prophet.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى أربعة إخوة من ثقيف، مسعود، وحبيب، وربيعة، وعبد ياليل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers addressed are Thaqif; they must fear God and leave the remaining usury, which was their claim, and accept the prohibition.
rows.anchor: { يأيها الذين آمنوا } ، يعنى ثقيفا، { اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا } الآية؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they refuse, “announce war” means expect war from God and His Messenger, which means unbelief; repentance requires abandoning the claim that usury is lawful.
rows.anchor: { فأذنوا } ، يعنى فاستيقنوا { بحرب من الله ورسوله } ، يعنى الكفر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On repentance, lenders may recover only their principal: adding to it wrongs debtors, while deducting from it wrongs the lenders.
rows.anchor: { فلكم رؤوس أموالكم } التي أسلفتم لا تزدادوا، { لا تظلمون } أحدا إذا لم تزدادوا على أموالكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet sent the verse to Attab, who read it to Banu Amr ibn Umayr; they repented and sought their principal, but Banu al-Mughira pleaded hardship, prompting the order to grant a debtor in hardship more time.
rows.anchor: فبعث النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذه الآية إلى عتاب بن أسيد بمكة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A debtor in hardship—here Banu al-Mughira—must be given time until becoming solvent; “grant me respite” in 7:14 means give me a delay.
rows.anchor: يعنى بنى المغيرة، { فنظرة إلى ميسرة } ، يقول: فأجله إلى غناه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiving the entire debt owed by insolvent Banu al-Mughira is better than collecting it.
rows.anchor: { وأن تصدقوا } به كله على بنى المغيرة وهم معسرون، فلا تأخذونه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about the Day of return means every righteous or wicked soul will receive the reward for its good and evil deeds without injustice.
rows.anchor: يعنى توفى { كل نفس } بر وفاجر ثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This was the last verse revealed in the Qur'an, and the Prophet died nine nights afterward.
rows.anchor: وهذه آخر أية نزلت من القرآن، ثم توفى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم بعدها بتسع ليال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing about the inhabitants of heaven or earth is hidden from God; everything is known to Him.
rows.anchor: يعنى شىء من أهل السماء، ولا من أهل الأرض، كل ذلك عنده،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about God's shaping people in wombs was revealed about Jesus, son of Mary, created without a father; God fashions male and female, well-formed and deformed, as He wills.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى عيسى ابن مريم صلى الله عليه وسلم، خلقه من غير أب، ذكرا وأنثى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is deity, mighty in His kingdom and wise in His command; the verse responds to the claims and calumny made about Jesus.
rows.anchor: فى ملكه، { الحكيم } [آية: 6] فى أمره، نزلت هذه الآية فى قولهم،
